verdict.rationale: Lithic's Authorization Rules v2 are configured once at program, account, or card level and then run server-side on every event. They cover card authorizations, 3DS, tokenization and ACH receipts, with no extra infrastructure, and offer shadow mode and backtesting, so they behave as narrow background automations. However, they are limited to approve/decline decisioning rather than general-purpose automations. ASA, webhooks, the MCP server and the agentic-commerce marketing are building blocks or interactive tools, not autonomous background automations, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: general-purpose workflow automations (scheduled or event-triggered actions beyond authorization decisioning), first-party automation builder documentation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
